methods.label: Complete the square
methods.explanation:
The fixed sum lets us express the product using one variable: \(y=1-x\). Completing the square then reveals a bound:
\[
xy=x(1-x)=\frac14-\left(x-\frac12\right)^2.
\]
For every real \(x\), the squared term is nonnegative, so \(xy\leq\tfrac14\). Equality is possible: taking \(x=y=\tfrac12\) satisfies \(x+y=1\) and gives \(xy=\tfrac14\). Thus the largest value is \(\boxed{0.25}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: An elementary square identity proves both the bound and its attainment for all real x and y.
